requirement:
Each listed file provides access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
rationale: structural: The text of `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` is: "Each listed file provides access to a file-notes view identifying its workspace-relative path." It has only one clause, and that clause describes what a user can observe. Each listed file gives access to a notes view, and that view identifies the file's workspace-relative path. The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface that the implementation must use or delegate to. I considered whether the clause could impose a structural obligation, such as a particular view type or link construction. Any alternative that keeps the same behavior still satisfies the text. Examples are a different link mechanism, a different view component, or building the path in a different place. So how the view is built is discretionary. No implementation roots were supplied, and none are needed. No structural obligation requires implementation evidence. Tests cover the observable behavior and are outside this criterion. behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation. Each listed file must give access to a file-notes view that shows the file's workspace-relative path. Two tests cover it. - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]` is marked as a test of this requirement. It covers three listed files: the root file `code.rs`, `src/direct.rs`, and the nested `src/deep/nested.rs`. For each file it takes the file's card in the index and asserts that the card has an `href` to the notes page. The expected link is built from `notes::path` and `chapter_href`. It also asserts per-note anchors such as `#coverage-note-N`. It then finds the book chapter named `File notes: {file}`, checks that its `path` equals the expected note path, and checks that its content contains `File: {file}`. That checks the workspace-relative path, including nested directories. Finally, it asserts that 5 `File notes:` chapters exist, which matches the five listed files, including `vendor/foreign.rs` and `docs_only/deep/item.rs`. The test also asserts that the unlisted `src/pass.rs` has no card. - `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs]` is also marked. It asserts that the rendered notes view contains `File: code.rs`. The path-identification and access-link obligations therefore have assertions on both sides: the link in the index and the path in the notes view. I found no obligation left without a test. The vendor and docs-only files are checked only for the existence of their notes pages, not for their path text. They go through the same page generation as the files checked in full, and the requirement draws no distinction for them.
